lil2-count-the-days-one-to-seven.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Can you count to seven with the days Yahweh made the world? Yes, you can! Yahweh made the world in six days, and on day seven He rested. One day for each finger, from one to seven. Let us count them together.
lil2-count-the-days-one-to-seven.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Can you count to seven with creation? Yes! Light was day one. Sky was day two. Land and trees, day three. Sun, moon and stars, day four. Fish and birds, day five. Animals and people, day six. Rest, day seven. One, two, three, four, five, six, seven. Seven days make one week. Yahweh counted the days, and now you can count them too.

teen.open: Can you count to seven using the days of creation? Yes. On each day Yahweh made something, and each day gets a number.
teen.close: So yes, you can count to seven with creation: light, sky, land, lights, fish and birds, animals and people, and rest. Seven days make one week.

senior.open: Can the days of creation teach a child to count to seven? They can: each day in Genesis 1 and 2 carries its own number, from light on day one to rest on day seven.
senior.close: So the title’s answer is yes. Day by day, one through seven, a child counts the week Yahweh made, and learns numbers and His work together.

lil4-sort-by-kind-two-by-two.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Can little hands sort like Yahweh does? Yes! Yahweh made each animal after its kind, so cows go with cows and birds go with birds. Then Noah brought them into the ark two by two. You can sort by kind and count by twos too.
lil4-sort-by-kind-two-by-two.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Can your little hands sort like Yahweh does? Yes, they can! Put things of the same kind together: cars with cars, blocks with blocks, animals with animals. Then count them two by two, like the animals going into the ark. Two, four, six, eight. You are sorting by kind, just the way Yahweh made them.

teen.open: Can you sort things the way Yahweh made them? Yes. Genesis says He made the animals by kind, and Noah brought them in two by two.
teen.close: So yes, you can sort like that. Group things by kind, then count them by twos, just like the animals going into the ark.

senior.open: Can a small child sort the way Yahweh ordered creation? Genesis shows Him making each creature after its kind, and Noah gathering them two by two.
senior.close: So the answer is yes. Sorting by kind and counting by twos both come straight from Genesis, and little hands can practise them with their own toys.

lil1-a-is-for-adam-who-named-the-animals.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Do you know the first letters? You will soon! Today you learn A, B and C, and each one comes from the Bible. A is for Adam. B is for bread. C is for cattle. Letters help you read His Word.
lil1-a-is-for-adam-who-named-the-animals.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Do you know the first letters now? Yes, you do! A is for Adam, who named the animals. B is for bread, that Jesus taught us to ask for. C is for cattle, that Yahweh made. A, B, C. Every letter you learn helps you read His Book. Say them one more time: A, B, C.

teen.open: Before you read a whole book, you start with letters. Here are the first three, A, B and C, each tied to the Bible.
teen.close: So now you know them: A for Adam, B for bread, C for cattle. Every letter you learn helps you read the Word.

senior.open: Before a child can read the Word, the child needs its letters. This lesson begins with A, B and C, each drawn from Scripture.
senior.close: So the title’s question is answered: A for Adam, B for bread, C for cattle. Three letters learned, and the first steps taken toward reading His Book.

Jesus said the mustard seed is one of the smallest seeds, but it grows into a big plant where birds sit. Today we measure a giant, see a little man climb a tree, and watch a tiny seed grow.
lil3-big-and-small-goliath-and-the-musta.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Can something tiny become something great? Yes! The mustard seed is smaller than a pea, and it grows so big that birds come and sit in its branches. Zacchaeus was little, and he climbed a tree to see Jesus. Small is not the end of the story. Yahweh made big things and small things, and He loves them all. He loves you too, big or small.

teen.open: Can something small turn into something big? Jesus said yes, using a tiny mustard seed that grows into a plant birds can rest in.
teen.close: So yes, tiny things can become great. A small seed becomes a big plant, a short man climbs to see Jesus, and Yahweh loves both big and small.

senior.open: Can something tiny become something great? Jesus answered with the mustard seed, the least of all seeds, which grows into a plant where the birds lodge.
senior.close: So the title’s answer is yes. The smallest seed becomes the greatest among herbs, and whether we are big or small, Yahweh made us and loves us.

lil7-adam-and-eve-made-loved-and-the-fir.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Did sin ruin everything, or did Yahweh already have a rescue plan? He had a plan. Adam and Eve broke the one rule, and that is sin. But Yahweh did not stop loving them, and He made them a promise that points to Jesus. Let us read the very first story.
lil7-adam-and-eve-made-loved-and-the-fir.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Did sin ruin everything? No. Sin was real, and Adam and Eve hid. But Yahweh came to them anyway. He made them clothes (Genesis 3:21). Then He promised that Someone would come and beat the liar (Genesis 3:15). That Someone is Jesus. Yahweh had a plan from the start, and His love did not stop. So when you do wrong, you can still run to Him.

teen.open: Did sin wreck everything, or did Yahweh already have a plan? He had a plan. Even right after Adam and Eve sinned, He kept loving them and made a promise that points to Jesus.
teen.close: So sin did not get the last word. Yahweh clothed Adam and Eve and promised Someone who would beat the liar. That Someone is Jesus, and His plan was there from the start.

senior.open: The title asks whether sin ruined everything, or whether Yahweh already had a rescue plan. The first story answers it: He kept loving Adam and Eve after they sinned, and in Genesis 3:15 He promised the One who would defeat the liar.
senior.close: So the answer is plain. Sin was real and costly, but it was not the end. Yahweh clothed Adam and Eve and gave the first promise, and that promise points to Jesus. He had a plan from the start.

Noah did build the ark and obey, but the saving was Yahweh's work from start to finish. Grace came first: Noah found grace before he built anything (Genesis 6:8). Then Yahweh closed the door and kept him. Here is the story.
lil8-noah-grace-the-door-yahweh-shut-and.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Why did Yahweh shut the door Himself? Because keeping Noah safe was His work. Grace is a gift, and Noah did not earn it. Noah obeyed and built, but Yahweh shut him in (Genesis 7:16), and the ark did not sink. Then Yahweh put His bow in the cloud. The same Yahweh who shut the door keeps His word. When you see a rainbow, say thank You.

teen.open: Why did Yahweh close the ark door Himself? To keep Noah safe. Noah found grace first, a gift he did not earn, and the saving was Yahweh's work.
teen.close: So Yahweh shut the door because keeping Noah safe was His job, not Noah's. And the rainbow says the same thing: Yahweh keeps His word.

senior.open: The title asks why Yahweh shut the door Himself. The story answers: Noah found grace before he built a single board (Genesis 6:8), and when the rain came, Yahweh Himself shut him in so he was safe.
senior.close: So the door tells us who did the saving. Noah obeyed in every detail, yet it was Yahweh who shut him in and kept him safe, and Yahweh who set the bow in the cloud. Grace came first, and He keeps His word.

lil6-how-many-loaves-how-many-baskets.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Can a little counting show us Yahweh's care? Yes, it can. Seven pieces of food fed a huge crowd, and twelve baskets were left over. Jesus made a little into a lot. The man with one hundred sheep went after the one that was lost, because that one mattered. And Yahweh counts the hairs on your head (Matthew 10:30). Every time you count, remember: He counts you, and you matter to Him.

teen.open: Can counting show how much Yahweh cares? Yes. Count the loaves, the baskets, the sheep, and you see a little become a lot and one lost sheep that mattered.
teen.close: So counting shows His care. Jesus turned seven pieces into twelve baskets left over, the shepherd went after the one, and Yahweh even counts the hairs on your head. You matter to Him.

senior.open: The title asks whether a little counting can show us Yahweh's care. It can. Each count in this lesson, the loaves, the baskets, the one lost sheep, the hairs of the head, points to how closely He provides and how much one person matters.
senior.close: So the counts carry the answer. Seven pieces fed a crowd with twelve baskets over; one sheep out of a hundred was sought; every hair is numbered (Matthew 10:30). Counting shows that Yahweh's care reaches to the smallest number, and to each of us.

You can start today with six small words that are all from His Book: light, good, day, night, made, love. Learn these, and you are already reading words from the Word. Let us learn them one at a time.
lil5-first-words-from-the-word.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Can little eyes read Yahweh's Word? Yes, and you just did. Light, good, day, night, made, love. Every one of these words comes from His Book. You found light in Genesis, made in Psalm 100, and love in 1 John. The best word is love, because He is love. Keep learning words, and one day you can read His Word all by yourself.

teen.open: Can a young reader read Yahweh's Word? Yes. Start with six words that all come from the Bible: light, good, day, night, made, love.
teen.close: So yes, you can read His Word. These six words are your start, and every one comes straight from His Book. Keep going and you will read it on your own.

senior.open: The title asks whether little eyes can read Yahweh's Word. They can, and this lesson shows the way in: six first words, light, good, day, night, made and love, each found in a verse of Scripture.
senior.close: So the answer is yes. A child who learns these six words is already reading words from the Word, and each one teaches something true: He made the light, He made us, and He is love. That is a good first step toward reading His Word alone.

lil9-abraham-the-promise-the-stars-and-t.open: THE QUESTION IN THE TITLE. Nobody can count the stars, so why did Abraham believe? Because he trusted Yahweh, the One who made the promise. He did not need to count it. He was old and had no children yet, but he believed Him (Genesis 15:6). And Yahweh did what He said. Let us walk with Abraham.
lil9-abraham-the-promise-the-stars-and-t.close: BACK TO THE QUESTION. Nobody can count the stars, so why did Abraham believe? He believed because Yahweh said it, and he trusted Yahweh. Then Yahweh kept His word. Isaac was born, just as He had spoken. On the hill, Abraham said Yahweh would provide the lamb, and Yahweh did. teen.open: If nobody can count the stars, why did Abraham believe Yahweh's promise? Because he trusted the One who promised, not his own counting.
teen.close: So Abraham believed because he trusted Yahweh. And Yahweh came through: Isaac was born, and on the hill Yahweh provided the lamb. He tells us, we believe Him, and He gives.

senior.open: The title asks why Abraham believed a promise as large as the stars he could not count. The answer is that his trust rested on Yahweh who spoke it, and the Word says he believed in the LORD (Genesis 15:6).
senior.close: So Abraham believed because Yahweh had spoken, not because he could see how. Yahweh kept that promise with Isaac, and on the hill He provided the lamb. Yahweh speaks, we believe Him, and He gives.
